What are bristles on a brush, and where else do you find them?

Bristles are short, stiff hairs, such as those on a toothbrush or on some animals. It is a noun, the plural of bristle.
Example: The bristles of the new brush were soft and white.
He came home bruised. What does that tell me?

Bruised means having a dark mark on the skin where it was hit, without any break in the skin. It is an adjective.
Example: Arun's knee was bruised after he fell off the swing.
Ceremonial dress: how is that different from normal dress?

Ceremonial means used for or connected with a formal event or ritual, so ceremonial dress is clothing worn for such events, not everyday wear. It is an adjective.
Example: The ceremonial procession moved slowly through the gates of the temple.
The toast was charred. Does that mean badly burnt?

Yes. Charred means burnt black on the surface. It is an adjective here.
Example: The charred wood in the fireplace was all that was left of the fire.
What does it mean to be choking, in the sense of food getting stuck?

Choking means being unable to breathe properly because something blocks the throat. It is a verb in its -ing form.
Example: The boy kept coughing and choking until the water went down.
I came across clergyman in a Victorian story. Please explain it.

A clergyman is a man who is trained and chosen for religious work in a Christian church. It is a noun, and the plural is clergymen.
Example: The clergyman greeted the villagers at the church door.
Mina complimented my drawing. Is complimented the same as flattered?

Not quite. Complimented means said something kind and admiring about someone or something. It is a verb, the past tense of compliment.
Example: The teacher complimented Kunal on his neat handwriting.
Is there more than one way to understand dinners?

The word has one basic meaning. Dinners are the main meals of the day, usually eaten in the evening. It is a noun, the plural of dinner.
Example: On weekends, the family cooks big dinners together.
I get distracted easily. Explain distract, please.

To distract means to take someone's attention away from what they are doing. It is a verb.
Example: Loud music can distract you while you are doing homework.
Disturbing has two sides, I think. Which is common in news stories?

In news stories, disturbing usually means upsetting or worrying. It is an adjective. As a verb, to disturb also means to interrupt someone.
Example: The disturbing report made many readers worried.
Which team is dominant? It is a phrase from our sports commentary.

Dominant means having more power, influence or success than the others. It is an adjective.
Example: The dominant team scored five goals before half time.
Whose downfall are we talking about in my history book? What does the word mean?

A downfall is a sudden loss of power, success or position. It is a noun.
Example: Pride was the king's downfall in the old story.
Enduring friendship: what's the key word here?

Enduring means lasting for a long time. It is an adjective.
Example: Their enduring friendship began in the first grade and continues today.
Why would a student get expelled? I need the word meaning as well.

Expelled means officially made to leave a school or group, usually for bad behaviour. It is a verb, the past tense of expel.
Example: The boy was expelled from the club for breaking the rules again and again.
Mum said the festivities begin on Friday. What exactly begins?

Festivities are the happy events and celebrations that take place at a festival or special occasion. It is a noun, usually plural.
Example: The festivities included music, dancing and a feast in the village square.
What were fortresses used for?

Fortresses were strong, well-guarded buildings or towns built to resist attack. It is a noun, the plural of fortress.
Example: Hill fortresses protected the towns below from enemy armies.
Our hostel warden is known for her friendliness. Which kind of word is this?

Friendliness is the quality of being kind and pleasant to others. It is a noun.
Example: The friendliness of the shopkeeper made new customers feel at home.
My teacher said that stories pass down through generations. What does the word generations mean?

Generations are groups of people born and living around the same time, or the time between one such group and the next. It is a noun, the plural of generation.
Example: Three generations of her family lived in the same house.
What is a grimace?

A grimace is a twisted expression on the face that shows pain, dislike or disgust. It is a noun. It can also be a verb.
Example: Leo made a grimace when he tasted the bitter medicine.
Why is everyone grumbling about the canteen queue?

Grumbling means complaining in a low, unhappy voice. It is a verb in its -ing form.
Example: The students were grumbling about the long queue at the canteen.
Would a harmonious family fight a lot?

No. Harmonious means peaceful and friendly, without disagreement. It is an adjective. It can also describe sounds that go well together.
Example: The two sisters have a harmonious relationship and rarely argue.
My granny describes me as headstrong. Is that a bad thing?

It can be mixed. Headstrong means determined to do things your own way and not wanting to listen to advice. It is an adjective.
Example: The headstrong horse refused to follow the path the rider chose.
What does massive mean when we say a massive tree?

Massive means very large, heavy and solid. It is an adjective.
Example: A massive banyan tree stood in the middle of the village.
The eggs hatched this morning. How is that different from just cracking?

Hatched means that the young animal inside came out of the egg; cracking only means the shell breaks. It is a verb, the past tense of hatch.
Example: Three tiny chicks hatched on the farm this morning.
Is a heroine a girl hero or something more?

She is a girl or woman admired for her courage, or the main female character in a story. It is a noun.
Example: The heroine of the novel saves her village from the flood.
Whats hissing? Like a snake?

Yes, like a snake. Hissing is making a long, sharp 'sss' sound. It is a verb in its -ing form.
Example: The kettle was hissing on the stove before the water boiled.
In a history passage, 'the ascendency of the king' appeared. How would you put ascendency?

Ascendency is a position of power or influence over others. It is a noun, and a formal one.
Example: The captain gained ascendency over the team after the final.
In the epic, he set out avenging his brother. What is avenging?

Avenging means punishing someone for harm done to another person, usually the person you love. It is a verb in its -ing form.
Example: The hero left home avenging the wrongs done to his family.
The queen was bestowing medals on the soldiers. What is that action?

Bestowing means giving something as an honour or gift. It is a verb in its -ing form.
Example: The principal was bestowing prizes on the winners of the quiz.
A blissful holiday: please explain blissful.

Blissful means full of great happiness and peace. It is an adjective.
Example: They spent a blissful week by the lake.
Does the fog dissipate on its own?

Yes. To dissipate means to spread out and slowly disappear. It is a verb.
Example: The morning mist began to dissipate as the sun climbed higher.
Someone gave me an equivocal answer. Why is it hard to trust?

Equivocal means unclear or having more than one possible meaning, so it is hard to be sure what is meant. It is an adjective.
Example: His equivocal reply left us unsure whether he would come.
What sort of amount is inordinate?

Inordinate means much greater than is usual or reasonable. It is an adjective, and it is formal.
Example: He spent an inordinate amount of time on one small drawing.
In the chapter, her life was irrevocably changed. What is the key adverb about?

Irrevocably means in a way that cannot be undone or turned back. It is an adverb.
Example: The decision irrevocably changed the course of the story.
When a character in a novel is called profligate, what is the writer saying?

Profligate describes someone who wastes things, especially money, in a careless way. It is an adjective.
Example: The profligate young heir spent his whole fortune in a year.
Was something stolen if it was purloined?

Yes, in a way. Purloined means stolen, usually something small, and it is a formal or humorous word. It is a verb, the past tense of purloin.
Example: Someone purloined the last biscuit from the tin.
Do I relinquish a seat when I give it up?

Yes. To relinquish means to give something up or let go of it, especially when you have to. It is a verb.
Example: The king had to relinquish his throne to his son.
Meera felt slighted when she was not invited. What was it she felt?

Slighted means treated as if you were not important, in a way that hurts your feelings. It is an adjective here.
Example: He felt slighted when no one asked for his opinion.
Is tresses another word for hair?

Yes, mostly. Tresses are long locks of hair, especially a woman's. It is a noun, used mainly in poetry and old stories.
Example: Her dark tresses fell over her shoulders as she bent over the book.
Can you tell me why a spiteful remark hurts?

Spiteful means done to hurt or annoy someone on purpose, out of unkind feelings, which is why it hurts. It is an adjective.
Example: It was spiteful of her to hide her sister's shoes.
The form has an additional page at the back. Does additional just mean extra?

Yes, it means extra or added to what you already have. It is an adjective.
Example: The shop charges an additional fee for delivery after eight in the evening.
What is anatomy? Our science teacher said we start it next term.

Anatomy is the study of the parts of a body and how they are arranged, in people, animals or plants. It is a noun.
Example: In anatomy class, Divya learned the names of the bones in the hand.
If someone looks apologetic, are they actually saying sorry?

Not always in words. Apologetic means showing that you feel sorry for something, often by your face or voice. It is an adjective.
Example: The waiter was apologetic about the long wait and brought us water at once.
How do I use appreciative in a thank-you note?

Appreciative means feeling or showing thanks for something good. It is an adjective, so it describes a person or a word like "smile" or "audience".
Example: We were very appreciative of the neighbours who watered our plants.
Mum asked about the seating arrangement for the party. What does she mean?

An arrangement is the way things or people are placed in order, or a plan made in advance. It is a noun. Your mum means where each guest will sit.
Example: The flower arrangement on the table was red and yellow.
Is artificial the opposite of natural?

Mostly, yes. Artificial means made by people rather than found in nature, often as a copy of something real. It is an adjective.
Example: The artificial flowers on the shelf never need water.
Someone said my cousin is very artistic. Is that about drawing only?

No, it is wider. Artistic means having skill or taste in making things such as paintings, music, dance or design. It is an adjective.
Example: Rehan is artistic, so he designed the stage for our school play.
Can you explain to astonish in plain words?

To astonish someone is to surprise them very much. It is a verb.
Example: Her sudden high jump astonished the whole class.
Is astronomy the same as astrology?

No. Astronomy is the science of stars, planets and space. Astrology is a different thing, a belief that stars affect people's lives, and it is not science. Astronomy is a noun.
Example: Our astronomy club meets on the roof to watch the moon.
Why do people say a tree is in blossom?

Blossom is the flowers on a tree, especially before the fruit grows, so a tree in blossom is covered in flowers. It is a noun. It can also be a verb meaning to start to flower or to grow well.
Example: The mango trees along our street are in blossom this month.
Is a builder only someone who makes houses?

Mostly yes, but not only. A builder is a person whose job is to build or repair houses and other buildings. It is a noun.
Example: The builder fixed the broken wall before the rains came.
A butcher's shop opened near us. What does a butcher do?

A butcher is a person who cuts and sells meat. It is a noun.
Example: The butcher wrapped the chicken in paper and tied it with string.
Which part of a cabbage do we eat, and is it a fruit?

We eat the thick round head of leaves, and it is a vegetable, not a fruit. Cabbage is a noun.
Example: Mina's grandmother cooked cabbage with peas for lunch.
What is cardboard made of? I need some for a project.

Cardboard is thick, stiff paper that is used for boxes and for making models. It is a noun, and we do not usually say "a cardboard" for the material.
Example: We cut a piece of cardboard into the shape of a boat.
Is charcoal the same as coal?

Not quite. Charcoal is a black material made by burning wood slowly with little air, used for cooking fires and for drawing. Coal is dug from the ground. Charcoal is a noun.
Example: Our neighbour grills corn on a charcoal fire every evening.
What colour is chestnut, and is it also a nut?

Both. A chestnut is a kind of nut that grows in a prickly case and is often roasted. It is also a reddish-brown colour, like the nut's skin. It is a noun, and as a colour it can also be an adjective.
Example: The girl brushed her chestnut hair before the photo.
The notice said it was a circular. How is that a noun?

As a noun, a circular is a printed notice or letter sent to many people at once. As an adjective, circular means shaped like a circle.
Example: The school sent a circular to every parent about the holiday.
How do I remember what circumference means for maths class?

Circumference is the distance all the way around a circle. It is a noun. Think of walking once round the edge of a round field.
Example: We wrapped a string around the tin to find its circumference.
Does civilization mean a country or a time in history?

It can mean a society at a certain time and place that has cities, writing and organized government, such as an ancient river-valley civilization. It can also mean human society in general. It is a noun.
Example: The museum has a map of an early civilization that lived near the river.
What does classification mean in a science book?

Classification is the sorting of things into groups according to what they have in common. It is a noun.
Example: The classification of animals into mammals, birds and reptiles helps us study them.
Is cleanse a fancy word for wash?

A little. To cleanse is to clean something thoroughly, often a wound, the skin or a place. It is a verb and sounds more formal than "wash".
Example: She cleansed the cut with clean water before putting a plaster on it.
My American friend says she sleeps under a comforter. What is it?

A comforter, in American English, is a thick, soft bed cover filled with warm stuffing. It is a noun. It can also mean a person or thing that brings comfort.
Example: Isha pulled her comforter up to her chin on the cold night.
Can I call my school friend a comrade?

You could, but it sounds serious or old-fashioned. A comrade is a friend or companion who shares work, a team or a struggle with you. It is a noun.
Example: The soldiers sat down to share their meal with a fellow comrade.
My teacher asked us to write a composition. Is it a story only?

No. A composition is a piece of writing on a topic, or a piece of music or art that someone created. It is a noun. Your teacher means a short essay or story.
Example: Our composition for tomorrow is about a day at the beach.
Is a contemporary writer someone who is alive now?

Usually yes, though not always. Contemporary means belonging to the present time, or to the same time as someone else. It is an adjective.
Example: The museum has an exhibition of contemporary art by young painters.
Is it rude to contradict my elder in a talk?

It can sound rude if you do it sharply. To contradict someone is to say the opposite of what they have said. It is a verb. You can disagree politely by saying, "I thought it was different. May I explain?"
Example: The two witnesses contradicted each other about the colour of the car.
What does correspond mean in a letter and in a maths question?

It has two meanings. To correspond can mean to match or be similar, as in "the numbers correspond". It also means to write letters to each other. It is a verb.
Example: Her answers did not correspond with the key at the back of the book.
How would I describe a crackle in a story?

A crackle is a quick series of small sharp sounds, such as a fire makes. It is a noun, and it is also a verb.
Example: We sat around the fire and listened to the crackle of the dry wood.
Is a crystal always clear like glass?

No. A crystal is a solid whose tiny parts are arranged in a regular pattern, and many are clear, but some are coloured. It is a noun. Salt and sugar are made of crystals too.
Example: The teacher showed us a salt crystal under a magnifying glass.
What does culture mean when people say "Indian culture"?

Culture means the way of life, customs, art, food, music and beliefs shared by a group of people. It is a noun.
Example: At the fair, each stall showed the food and dance of a different culture.
Is a currant a berry? I saw it on a cake box.

A currant is a small dried grape, or a small round berry that grows on a bush. It is a noun. The dried type is common in cakes and buns.
Example: Mum put a handful of currants into the bun dough.
Is it customary to take off shoes when you go to a temple? What does the word say?

Yes, in many places it is. Customary means usual or expected because of tradition or habit. It is an adjective.
Example: It is customary to greet the elders first when you enter the room.
Declaration is on our customs form. What are they asking?

A declaration is a formal statement, such as telling officials what you are carrying or stating facts in writing. It is a noun.
Example: The traveller filled in a declaration listing the items in his bag.
The headline said "a new development in the case". Which sense is that?

Here development means a new event or step that changes a situation. It is a noun. It can also mean growth, as in the development of a child.
Example: There was an exciting development when the lost dog was found at the station.
Why is diamond called the hardest stone? Also what part of speech is it?

A diamond is a very hard, clear, precious stone, which is why people use it for jewels and for cutting tools. It is a noun. It can also be a shape with four equal sides.
Example: She wore a ring with a small diamond.
Who is a director in a film and in a company?

A director is a person who leads or manages something. In a film, the director decides how the story is shown. In a company, a director is a senior manager. It is a noun.
Example: The director asked the actors to repeat the scene.
Parents sometimes disapprove of something. Does it mean they are angry?

Not necessarily. To disapprove is to think that something is wrong or not good, without always being angry. It is a verb, and we usually say "disapprove of".
Example: Her father disapproved of the late-night party but did not shout.
What happens if you disobey a rule?

To disobey is to not do what you are told or what a rule says. It is a verb. What happens depends on the rule and who made it.
Example: The boy disobeyed the sign and walked on the wet grass.
Can a gift displease someone?

Yes. To displease someone is to make them annoyed or unhappy. It is a verb.
Example: The loud music displeased the neighbours.
What is distribution in a shop or in a class?

Distribution is the act of giving out or spreading things among people or places. It is a noun.
Example: The distribution of sweets will take place after the assembly.
Is a document only something on paper?

No. A document is a piece of written or printed information, on paper or on a computer, that gives facts or proof. It is a noun. It can also be a verb meaning to record.
Example: Please bring a document with your name and address on it.
Can downhill be used for a bike ride and a bad situation?

Yes. Downhill means going down a slope. It is an adverb or an adjective. If things go downhill, they get worse.
Example: The cyclist rode downhill with the wind behind him.
What does a drummer do in a band?

A drummer is a person who plays the drums, keeping the beat for the rest of the band. It is a noun.
Example: The drummer counted four beats and the song began.
What is efficiency? It is in the notice about the new machine.

Efficiency means doing a job well without wasting time, effort or money. It is a noun.
Example: The new dishwasher works with great efficiency and uses little water.
Is elementary the same as easy? I know there is an elementary school too.

Close. Elementary means basic or simple, dealing with the first steps. It is an adjective. An elementary school is for the youngest pupils in some countries.
Example: She learned the elementary rules of chess in an afternoon.
Can I embrace an idea as well as a person?

Yes. To embrace someone is to hug them. To embrace an idea is to accept it gladly. It is a verb, and it can also be a noun for a hug.
Example: The two friends embraced at the airport after a long time.
What is embroidery, and do I need a machine for it?

Embroidery is decorative sewing, making patterns on cloth with a needle and coloured thread. It is a noun. You can do it by hand or by machine.
Example: Her grandmother's embroidery on the scarf shows tiny red birds.
Is something enjoyable the same as exciting?

Not quite. Enjoyable means giving pleasure, which can be calm or lively. Exciting means causing strong interest or thrill. It is an adjective.
Example: Our walk by the river was quiet and enjoyable.
How do you enlarge a photo, and does the word work for rooms too?

To enlarge something is to make it bigger. It is a verb, and it works for photos, rooms or any other thing.
Example: We enlarged the picture so it would fit the frame on the wall.
Our class talked about equality today. What does that word cover?

Equality means being equal, with the same rights, chances and respect as everyone else. It is a noun.
Example: The club was started to give girls and boys equality on the cricket field.
Our teacher says to estimate the answer first. How is that different from guessing?

To estimate is to work out a rough value or amount using what you know, so it is more careful than a wild guess. It is a verb, and it is also a noun for the rough amount.
Example: Asha estimated that the walk to the market would take twenty minutes.
Why do pine trees get called evergreen?

Evergreen describes a plant that keeps green leaves all year instead of losing them in autumn. It is an adjective and also a noun for such a tree.
Example: Evergreen trees on the hill stayed green through the winter.
The poster says the show is exclusive to members. Does it mean good or closed?

Here exclusive means limited to a particular group, so only members can go. It is an adjective. It can also mean fancy and costly, but your poster means the first sense.
Example: The library has an exclusive reading room for teachers.
What does expansion mean when a shop talks about it?

Expansion is the act of becoming larger or spreading to more places. It is a noun. A shop with an expansion plan wants to get bigger.
Example: The bakery's expansion included a second shop near the bus stand.
My teacher called our project experimental. Is that good or bad?

It is neither. Experimental means new and still being tested, or based on experiments. It is an adjective.
Example: The band played an experimental song that mixed drums with the sound of rain.
Do you extinguish a candle or a fire, or both?

Both. To extinguish is to put out a fire or a light. It is a verb, and it sounds more formal than "put out".
Example: The fire fighters extinguished the fire in the empty shed.
Is eyesight the same as vision?

Yes, very nearly. Eyesight is the ability to see, and vision is another word for it. Eyesight is a noun.
Example: Grandfather's eyesight is so good that he can read the small print without glasses.
When a poet says foliage, does it mean one leaf?

No, it means all the leaves of a plant or tree together. It is a noun and is not used with "a".
Example: The thick foliage of the banyan tree kept the courtyard cool.
In art class we learned about the foreground of a picture. What is it?

The foreground is the part of a scene or picture that is nearest to the viewer. It is a noun. The part far away is the background.
Example: In the photo, two children sit in the foreground and the mountains rise behind them.
Why do teachers say we must learn the fundamental ideas first?

Fundamental means basic and most important, the part everything else depends on. It is an adjective.
Example: Learning to read is fundamental to every other subject.
Is gingerbread bread with ginger, or more like a cake?

It is closer to a cake or biscuit. Gingerbread is a sweet baked treat flavoured with ginger and often shaped into figures or houses. It is a noun.
Example: The children decorated gingerbread men with sugar for the Christmas party.
What is glitter? We are using it for the craft day.

Glitter is tiny shiny pieces used for decoration. It is a noun. As a verb, glitter means to shine with small flashes of light.
Example: Priya sprinkled glitter on the card and shook off the extra.
Does a godfather have a duty in the family?

In some traditions a godfather is a man who promises at a child's naming ceremony to help look after the child's learning and faith. It is a noun.
Example: Little Noah's godfather gave him a book on his birthday.
Can you describe a gooseberry for me? I have never seen one.

A gooseberry is a small round green or pale berry with a sour taste, used in jams and desserts. It is a noun.
Example: Grandmother made a jar of gooseberry pickle for the winter.
How big is a handful, and can I use it for people too?

A handful is as much as one hand can hold. It is a noun. It can also mean a small number, as in a handful of people.
Example: Only a handful of students stayed for the extra class.
Is heather a plant or a name?

It is both, but as a word in books it is a low shrub with tiny purple or pink flowers that grows on open hills. It is a noun. Heather is also used as a girl's name.
Example: The hills were covered with purple heather.
How is a historian different from a history teacher?

A historian studies and writes about the past, often by reading old records. A history teacher teaches the subject, though some do both. Historian is a noun.
Example: The historian visited the old fort to study its walls and stones.
Is honeymoon only a trip, or something else as well?

It is mainly the holiday a newly married couple takes after the wedding. It is a noun. It can also mean a short happy start of something new, as in a honeymoon period.
Example: Meena's aunt and uncle went to a hill station for their honeymoon.
What is the hillside, and is it the top or the slope?

It is the sloping side of a hill, not the top. It is a noun.
Example: Small houses were spread across the green hillside.
The quiz says: identify the bird in the picture. What am I being asked to do?

To identify something is to recognize it and say what it is or who it is. It is a verb.
Example: Can you identify the bird from its song?
Is it bad to imitate a friend?

Not always. To imitate is to copy the way someone acts, speaks or looks. It is a verb. It is fine as practice or fun, but copying someone's work and calling it yours is not fine.
Example: The parrot can imitate the sound of the doorbell.
Are there immortal creatures in real life? And what does it mean?

Immortal means living forever and never dying. It is an adjective. Nothing alive on Earth is known to be immortal, but the idea is common in stories.
Example: In the legend, the hero drank a magic drink and became immortal.
What makes a result impressive?

Something is impressive when it makes people admire it because it is large, skilful or very good. It is an adjective.
Example: Her speech was impressive, and the whole hall applauded.
Can a volcano be inactive but not dead?

Yes. Inactive means not doing anything or not currently working or erupting. It is an adjective. An inactive volcano may erupt again, while an extinct one is not expected to.
Example: Our club was inactive in the rainy season.
Is incorrect rude to say to a classmate?

It can sound cold if said sharply, but the word itself is fine. Incorrect means wrong or not true. It is an adjective. You may soften it by saying, "I think that one is not quite right."
Example: He circled the incorrect answer and tried again.
What is an indication? Someone said dark clouds are an indication of rain.

An indication is a sign that shows something is true or likely to happen. It is a noun. Dark clouds are an indication of rain.
Example: There was no indication that the train would be late.
I saw inflammable on a gas can. Is it safe or the opposite?

It is a warning. Inflammable means able to catch fire easily, exactly the same as flammable. It is an adjective, and the "in" does not make it negative here.
Example: Keep the inflammable liquid far from the stove.
Does for instance mean the same as for example?

Yes. Instance is a noun meaning one example or case, so for instance is another way of saying for example.
Example: Many birds eat insects. The sparrow, for instance, feeds its chicks with them.
Who was the first inventor, and what does the word mean?

Nobody knows who was first. An inventor is a person who creates something new, such as a machine or a tool. It is a noun.
Example: The inventor of the small pump built it in his garage.
What is invisible in a story, and is it the same as hidden?

Invisible means that cannot be seen. It is an adjective. It is not exactly hidden, since something hidden is out of sight on purpose and could still be seen.
Example: The gas is invisible, but you can smell it.
The police will investigate the missing bicycle. What do they do?

To investigate is to look carefully into something to find out the facts. It is a verb.
Example: The teacher investigated why the classroom window was broken.
Can a sound really irritate you, or is that just a saying?

To irritate someone is to make them slightly angry or annoyed. It is a verb. It can also mean to make a part of the body sore.
Example: The constant tapping on the desk began to irritate the teacher.
On the road sign, what is a junction?

A junction is a place where two or more roads, tracks or lines meet. It is a noun.
Example: Turn left at the junction near the petrol pump.
Is a keyhole the hole the key goes into, and where does the phrase come from?

Yes, a keyhole is the small hole in a lock where you put the key. It is a noun.
Example: The little boy peeked through the keyhole to see who was knocking.
What part of the hand is a knuckle?

A knuckle is a joint of the finger, especially the bump where the finger joins the hand. It is a noun.
Example: He knocked on the door with his knuckle.
Is a landowner always rich?

Not necessarily. A landowner is a person who owns land, big or small. It is a noun.
Example: The landowner rented the field to a young farmer.
My teacher said my handwriting is barely legible. What is she asking for?

Legible means clear enough to read. It is an adjective. She is asking you to write more neatly.
Example: Write your name in legible letters so that the examiner can read it.
Can you liberate an animal and a country?

Yes. To liberate is to set free. It is a verb, and it works for animals, people or places.
Example: The villagers liberated the bird from the net.
What is a locksmith?

A locksmith is a person who makes, fits and repairs locks and keys. It is a noun.
Example: We called a locksmith when the key broke inside the door.
Does majority mean more than half?

Yes. The majority is the larger part of a group, more than half. It is a noun.
Example: The majority of the class voted for a picnic.
In a vote, what does minority mean?

Minority is the smaller part of a group, fewer than half. It is a noun. It can also mean a small group of people who differ from most in a country.
Example: Only a minority of the students wanted the extra homework.
Is manufacture only for factories?

Mostly. To manufacture is to make goods in large numbers, usually with machines. It is a verb.
Example: The company manufactures school bags in the town.
What does maximum mean on a lift sign?

Maximum means the greatest amount allowed or possible. It is an adjective or a noun. On a lift sign it tells you the most people or weight that is safe.
Example: The maximum number of people in this lift is six.
Is a mathematical problem a problem with numbers only?

Mostly, yes. Mathematical means connected with maths. It is an adjective. Shapes, patterns and logic problems can be mathematical too.
Example: Her mathematical skill helped her win the quiz.
Is a messenger the same as a postman?

Not quite. A messenger is a person who carries messages or parcels between people. A postman delivers the post as a regular job. Messenger is a noun.
Example: The messenger ran across the town with a note for the doctor.
Why do we say bird migration?

Migration is the movement of animals or people from one place to another, often each year. It is a noun. For birds it means flying to warmer places when the weather changes.
Example: Thousands of cranes passed over the lake during their autumn migration.
Is misunderstand the same as understand wrongly? Also, how is it used?

Yes. To misunderstand is to get the meaning wrong. It is a verb. People misunderstand when a message is not clear.
Example: I misunderstood the time and arrived an hour early.
What does moderate mean for weather, and can it be a verb?

As an adjective, moderate means neither too much nor too little, as in moderate rain. As a verb, it means to make something less strong, and it is spoken differently.
Example: The weatherman promised moderate winds for the sailing race.
Why was our school trip called a mission?

A mission is an important task or journey with a clear aim. It is a noun. Your teacher probably used it for fun to make the trip sound exciting.
Example: The scouts went on a mission to clean the beach.
Is a nickname an insult or a pet name?

It can be either, depending on the tone. A nickname is an informal name used by friends or family instead of a real name, often short or funny. It is a noun.
Example: Everyone calls Siddharth by his nickname, Sid.
Is an obstacle always something you can touch?

No. An obstacle is anything that blocks your way or makes it hard to do something, a real object or a problem. It is a noun.
Example: Fear of speaking was the biggest obstacle for Vikram in the debate.
Can an occurrence be good as well as bad?

Yes. An occurrence is something that happens, good or bad. It is a noun, and it often refers to events that happen now and then.
Example: Rain in April is a rare occurrence in this town.
Is a school an organization? And what does the word mean?

Yes. An organization is a group of people who work together for a purpose, such as a school, a club or a company. It is a noun. The same word also means the way something is arranged.
Example: A local organization collects books for children's libraries.
Does an ostrich really put its head in the sand, and what is it?

No, that is a myth. An ostrich is the largest bird in the world, tall with long legs and unable to fly, and it runs very fast. It is a noun.
Example: We saw an ostrich running across the field at the zoo.
My uncle has a positive outlook on life. What does it mean?

Outlook is a person's general way of thinking about things, or what is likely to happen later. It is a noun. A positive outlook means expecting good things.
Example: Her cheerful outlook helped the whole team after the loss.
The teacher said my story is overdone. Is that like overcooked?

Similar idea. Overdone means done too much, or cooked too long. It is an adjective. For a story it means it tries too hard or uses too many dramatic details.
Example: The rice was overdone and had turned soft and sticky.
Is a palette a board, or the colours on it?

Both senses are used. A palette is a thin board on which an artist mixes paint. It can also mean the range of colours that an artist uses. It is a noun.
Example: Kavya squeezed blue and yellow onto her palette to make green.
When we reach the top, you will get a panorama. What will I see?

A panorama is a wide view of a large area that you can see all at once. It is a noun.
Example: From the hilltop, we saw a panorama of fields and the river below.
Is parsley a herb or a spice?

It is a herb, the green leaves of a plant used to add flavour and decoration. Spices usually come from seeds, bark or roots. Parsley is a noun.
Example: Dad chopped some parsley and sprinkled it over the soup.
How is participate different from attend?

To participate is to take part in an activity, while to attend is just to be present. It is a verb.
Example: All the students participated in the sports day races.
Is a driver a passenger?

No. A passenger is a person who travels in a vehicle, train, plane or boat but is not driving or working on it. It is a noun.
Example: The passenger in the next seat offered me a window view.
What kind of land is pasture?

Pasture is land covered with grass where cattle, sheep or goats feed. It is a noun.
Example: The cows walked to the green pasture behind the village at dawn.
Is a pathway the same as a path or a road?

Almost. A pathway is a narrow way made for people to walk on, like a path. A road is wider and made for vehicles. Pathway is a noun.
Example: A stone pathway led to the front door of the old house.
Does patriotic mean you must always agree with your country?

No. Patriotic means loving your country and being proud of it. It is an adjective. A person can be patriotic and still want things in the country to improve.
Example: The children sang a patriotic song at the Republic Day programme.
What is a pedestal, and what does "put someone on a pedestal" say?

A pedestal is the base on which a statue or column stands. It is a noun. To put someone on a pedestal means to admire them so much that you forget their faults.
Example: The statue of the horse stood on a tall pedestal in the square.
Is a penknife only for sharpening pens?

Not now. A penknife is a small folding knife that fits in a pocket. It was once used to mend quill pens. It is a noun.
Example: The scout used his penknife to cut a stick for the tent.
Can anyone who acts in a school play be called a performer?

Yes. A performer is a person who entertains an audience by acting, singing, dancing or playing music. It is a noun.
Example: Every performer bowed when the curtain came down.
Is phenomenon the plural or singular? I get confused.

Phenomenon is the singular. The plural is phenomena. It is a noun meaning something that happens or exists and can be observed, often something unusual.
Example: A rainbow is a natural phenomenon caused by sunlight and water drops.
Was every pioneer a settler? I saw it in a history lesson.

No. A pioneer is a person who is among the first to try something new or to explore a new place. A settler is one who goes to live in a new area. Pioneer is a noun.
Example: She was a pioneer in teaching girls to code in her town.
Plumage is on a bird poster. What is that?

Plumage is all the feathers that cover a bird. It is a noun.
Example: The peacock spread his bright blue plumage in the garden.
Is porcelain just another name for china?

Mostly. Porcelain is a hard, thin, white ceramic material used for cups, plates and ornaments. China is another name for it. It is a noun.
Example: My grandmother keeps her porcelain tea set in a glass cupboard.
What does portable mean on a speaker box?

Portable means easy to carry or move from place to place. It is an adjective.
Example: He packed a portable fan in his bag for the train ride.
What is the postmark on a letter, and what does it tell me?

A postmark is a mark stamped on a letter by the post office, showing the place and date it was posted. It is a noun.
Example: The postmark on the envelope said the card was sent from Pune.
Poverty came up in a class talk. How would you explain it simply?

Poverty is the state of not having enough money for basic needs such as food, clothes and a home. It is a noun.
Example: Many charities work to reduce poverty in the villages.
Is a prairie a desert, a forest or a field?

A prairie is a large, flat area of grassland with few trees, mostly in North America. It is a noun.
Example: The old film shows wagons crossing the prairie.
Does precision mean the same as speed?

No. Precision means being exact and accurate, which can take time. It is a noun.
Example: The watchmaker worked with great precision, placing each tiny part exactly.
Who is a predecessor of a headmaster?

A predecessor is a person who held a job or position before someone else. It is a noun. The headmaster's predecessor is the one who was in the post earlier.
Example: Our new principal thanked her predecessor for the clean, happy school.
I have many things to do. Is the first one my priority, or is that something else?

Yes, you can call it your top priority. A priority is something that is more important than other things and should be dealt with first. It is a noun.
Example: Finishing the science project is my priority this weekend.
Why do people use the word pyramid for both buildings and shapes?

Because both look the same. A pyramid is a solid shape with a flat base and sloping sides that meet at a point at the top. The huge stone tombs in Egypt are called pyramids for their shape. It is a noun.
Example: We built a small pyramid out of clay for our history project.
Can I ask my teacher to reconsider my marks?

Yes, politely. To reconsider is to think again about a decision or an opinion. It is a verb. A teacher may or may not change the marks after checking.
Example: After hearing her friend's reasons, Neha reconsidered going on the trip.
Is recreation another word for sports?

Not only sports. Recreation is any activity done for enjoyment and rest, such as games, walks or hobbies. It is a noun.
Example: The park offers boating, cycling and other recreation for families.
Is a regulation a rule? Where do I see it?

Yes, mostly. A regulation is an official rule made by an authority, often about safety. It is a noun.
Example: A school regulation says students must wear helmets when they cycle to school.
Is a frog a reptile?

No. A frog is an amphibian. A reptile is a cold-blooded animal with scales that crawls or has short legs, such as a snake, lizard or turtle. Reptile is a noun.
Example: The zoo has a special house for reptiles, including a huge python.
How is resemble different from be like?

To resemble is to look or be similar to someone or something. It means almost the same as "be like" but sounds more formal. It is a verb, used without "to".
Example: Arun resembles his father, with the same smile and walk.
Does responsible mean the same as to blame?

Not exactly. Responsible can mean to blame for something that happened, but it also means being the person in charge of something, or being sensible and trustworthy. It is an adjective.
Example: Rhea is responsible for feeding the class fish each morning.
How can the Earth both revolve and rotate?

To revolve is to move in a circle around another object, which Earth does around the sun. To rotate is to spin on its own axis. Revolve is a verb.
Example: The moon revolves around the Earth about once a month.
Is rhythmic only used for music?

No. Rhythmic means having a regular, repeated pattern of sounds or movements, in music, dance, speech or even breathing. It is an adjective.
Example: The rhythmic clapping of the crowd kept the drummers in time.
Is a saucepan the same as a pot? I am helping in the kitchen.

Similar. A saucepan is a deep cooking pan, usually smaller than a pot, with a long handle and often a lid. It is a noun.
Example: Mum heated milk in a small saucepan.
Is a schoolroom the same as a classroom?

Mostly the same, but schoolroom sounds older, as in books about the past. It means a room in which lessons are taught. It is a noun.
Example: In the story, the children sat on wooden benches in a plain schoolroom.
Who makes a sculpture, and from what?

A sculptor makes it. A sculpture is a work of art in three dimensions, carved or shaped from stone, wood, metal or clay. It is a noun.
Example: A stone sculpture of an elephant stands outside the museum.
Why do ships and prisons have a searchlight?

A searchlight is a powerful lamp that can send a strong beam in any direction so that people can see far away at night. Ships use it to find things in the dark. It is a noun.
Example: The searchlight swept across the harbour to find the small boat.
Does shorthand mean a short form? Or is it a skill?

Both are right. Shorthand is a quick way of writing using symbols and short forms, used to write as fast as people speak. It is a noun. It can also mean any short way of saying something.
Example: The secretary took notes in shorthand during the meeting.
What is a shuttlecock and why does it have feathers?

A shuttlecock is the small light object with feathers or plastic that players hit in badminton. The feathers slow it down and make it fly straight. It is a noun.
Example: The shuttlecock got stuck in the tree after Rohan's smash.
Can I print my name as a signature?

Not really. A signature is your name written in your own style by hand, used to show that a document is yours. Printed names are usually not signatures. It is a noun.
Example: Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
What does significant mean when a graph is described?

Significant means important or large enough to matter. It is an adjective.
Example: There was a significant rise in the number of visitors during the festival.
Is a skylight a window in the sky? It sounds odd to me.

It sounds that way, but a skylight is a window set into a roof or ceiling to let daylight in. It is a noun.
Example: Sunshine came through the skylight and lit the kitchen.
I got a splinter from the bench. What is it and what do people do?

A splinter is a thin sharp piece of wood, glass or metal that has broken off a bigger piece. It is a noun. For one in your skin, an adult or a nurse can help take it out.
Example: A splinter from the old fence stuck in Tara's finger.
Can music stimulate your brain, or is that just a saying?

To stimulate is to make something become more active or interested. It is a verb. Music can stimulate thinking and feeling, though the effects depend on the person.
Example: The teacher used pictures to stimulate the children's interest in the topic.
Is a stretcher a bed? We saw one at the station.

It is a light frame or bed with handles used to carry a sick or injured person. It is a noun.
Example: Two helpers carried the injured player off the field on a stretcher.
Is despise stronger than dislike?

Yes, much stronger. To despise someone or something is to feel that it is worthless and to dislike it very strongly. It is a verb.
Example: The villagers despised the cruel landlord who took their crops.
A leader said she would denounce the dumping of waste. What will she do?

To denounce is to say publicly that something is wrong or evil. It is a verb.
Example: The mayor denounced the dumping of rubbish in the river.
Is enchantment only used for magic in fairy tales?

Mostly, but not only. Enchantment is the effect of a magic spell, or a feeling of great delight and charm. It is a noun.
Example: The children watched the puppet show with enchantment.
What counts as a garment? Is a shoe one?

A garment is any piece of clothing, such as a shirt, skirt or coat. It is a noun. Shoes are footwear, not garments.
Example: Each garment in the shop had a small paper tag with its price.
A book calls a house genteel. Is that praise?

In the book it describes a house as polite and respectable in an old-fashioned way. Today genteel is an adjective used a little jokingly for someone who is too refined and proper.
Example: The genteel old lady served tea in thin china cups.
Can a gleeful laugh be a bad thing?

Usually it is happy, but it can also be unkind if someone enjoys another person's trouble. Gleeful means full of joy and excitement. It is an adjective.
Example: The children let out a gleeful shout when the rain stopped play.
Is a harpoon a spear or a gun?

It is a long spear with a rope tied to it, used for catching large fish and sea animals. It is a noun, and in modern times many people think whale hunting with it is cruel.
Example: The old museum has a rusty harpoon from a fishing ship.
Does heroism need a big act, like saving a life?

No. Heroism is great courage and goodness in difficult moments, and it can be small too. It is a noun.
Example: The firefighter was praised for his heroism in the flood.
How is implore different from ask?

To implore is to beg someone strongly and in a serious way. It is a verb and is much stronger than ask.
Example: The boy implored his mother to let him keep the stray kitten.
If a noise is intolerable, can you still be polite about it?

Yes. Intolerable means so bad that you cannot put up with it. It is an adjective. You can say politely, "The noise is becoming hard for me to bear. Could we lower it?"
Example: The heat in the room was intolerable, so we opened every window.
Is a lattice a fence or a pattern?

It is both. A lattice is a frame of crossed strips of wood or metal, with open spaces between them. It is a noun and is often used for plants to climb on.
Example: Green beans grew up the wooden lattice at the side of the house.
Is lethargic the same as lazy?

Not really. Lethargic means tired and slow, with no energy, often because of heat, illness or boredom. Lazy means not wanting to work. Lethargic is an adjective.
Example: The heat made the whole class feel lethargic after lunch.
Can you be mortified by a small mistake?

Yes. To mortify someone is to make them feel very embarrassed or ashamed. It is a verb, and it is often used in the passive, as in "I was mortified".
Example: Ravi was mortified when his phone rang during the quiet assembly.
Are all night animals nocturnal?

Yes, for the animals that are active at night and sleep during the day. Nocturnal is an adjective. Owls and bats are examples.
Example: Bats are nocturnal, so you see them only at dusk.
The sign says do not obstruct the gate. What does obstruct mean here?

To obstruct is to block a path, view or process so that something cannot get through or move. It is a verb. A sign like that asks you not to leave anything in the way.
Example: A parked lorry obstructed the narrow lane.
Can a penitent person still make the same mistake?

They may, but a penitent person is sorry for what they did and wants to do better. Penitent is an adjective. It is a formal word, often found in books about faith.
Example: The penitent boy returned the stolen pencil and apologized.
Does perplex mean to confuse?

Yes, in a deep way. To perplex is to puzzle someone so much that they cannot work out the answer. It is a verb.
Example: The riddle perplexed the whole class for a week.
Does plaintive describe a sad voice or a sad person?

It describes a sound, often a voice or a song, that sounds sad and a little like crying. It is an adjective.
Example: We heard the plaintive call of a lost lamb.
Is a prophecy a prediction I can trust?

Not always. A prophecy is a statement about what will happen in the future, often made through religion or magic. It is a noun. There is no sure way to check one in advance.
Example: In the old tale, a prophecy said a boy would become king.
Is reticent the same as shy?

Close, but not identical. Reticent means not eager to share your thoughts or feelings. A reticent person may be quiet for any reason, not only shyness. It is an adjective.
Example: He was reticent about his plans and only smiled when asked.
Is scoundrel a very rude word?

It is rude, but also old-fashioned. A scoundrel is a dishonest or wicked person. It is a noun. You will meet it mostly in old books and films.
Example: In the story, the scoundrel tried to cheat the villagers of their harvest.
A taciturn person at a party: how would you describe them?

A taciturn person is quiet by nature and says very little. It is an adjective. At a party, they may stand at the side and listen.
Example: The taciturn watchman rarely said more than good morning.
In an old book it says she upbraided him. Is that praise or a scolding?

It is a scolding. To upbraid someone is to tell them off in a stern way for something they did. It is a verb and is rarely used today.
Example: The mother upbraided her son for coming home late without a call.
Is venerable a polite way of saying old?

Yes. Venerable describes an old person or thing that is respected because of age and wisdom or history. It is an adjective.
Example: The venerable old teacher was greeted warmly by his former pupils.
Is vexation the same as anger?

Not quite. Vexation is the feeling of being annoyed or troubled by something, usually milder than anger. It is a noun and a rather old-fashioned word.
Example: To her great vexation, the bus drove away just as she reached the stop.
Would you call a baby winsome?

You could. Winsome means attractive in a sweet, charming way. It is an adjective, and it is a bit old-fashioned.
Example: The winsome little girl waved at everyone on the bus.
How are wrinkle in a shirt and wrinkle on the skin the same?

They are the same idea. A wrinkle is a small line or fold, in cloth or on the skin. It is a noun. As a verb, to wrinkle is to make or get such folds.
Example: Dad pressed the wrinkle out of his shirt before the meeting.
Can a plant be thirsty or only a person?

People say a plant is thirsty as a way of saying it needs water. Thirsty means wanting or needing a drink. It is an adjective.
Example: After the football match, the players were hot and thirsty.
Is threaten always about people, or can weather threaten too?

Both. To threaten is to say you will hurt or harm someone, or, for things like weather, to seem likely to cause trouble. It is a verb.
Example: Dark clouds threatened to spoil the picnic.
Is toothache one word? What does it mean?

Yes, one word. Toothache is a pain in a tooth. It is a noun.
Example: Maya stayed home from school because of a bad toothache.
Is waterproof the same as water-resistant?

Not exactly. Waterproof means that water cannot pass through at all. Water-resistant means it keeps out some water but not all. Waterproof is an adjective.
Example: He wore a waterproof jacket on the wet trek.
How does a whirlpool form, and is it dangerous?

A whirlpool is a place in water where the water spins around fast, often where currents meet. It is a noun. It can be dangerous for swimmers, so keep away from one.
Example: The boat went around the whirlpool in the river.
Is wealthy the same as rich?

Yes, very close. Wealthy means having a lot of money or property. It is an adjective and sounds a bit more formal than rich.
Example: The wealthy merchant gave a large sum to build the school library.
What is vinegar, and why does it taste sour?

Vinegar is a sour liquid made from wine or fruit juice that has turned sour, used on salads and in pickles. It tastes sour because of an acid in it. It is a noun.
Example: She added a spoon of vinegar to the salad.
Is tradition always old?

Mostly. A tradition is a custom or belief passed from one generation to the next. It is a noun. A new custom can become a tradition if people keep doing it year after year.
Example: Lighting lamps at the door is a tradition in our family at Diwali.
Is it traveler or traveller? I see both.

Both are correct. Traveler is the usual spelling in American English, and traveller is used in British and Indian English. It is a noun for a person who goes on a journey.
Example: The tired traveler stopped at a roadside tea shop.
Is my surname my family name or last name?

They are the same. Your surname is the family name you share with your relatives, usually the last part of your full name. It is a noun.
Example: Please write your first name and your surname on the form.
Is a sunbeam just a ray of sun?

Yes. A sunbeam is a narrow line of sunlight. It is a noun.
Example: A sunbeam came through the curtain and fell on the sleeping cat.
How do I make a suggestion without sounding bossy?

A suggestion is an idea you offer for others to think about. It is a noun. To avoid sounding bossy, start with "Maybe we could" or "What if we".
Example: Her suggestion to start the project early helped everyone.
In football, what is a substitute, and is it a verb as well?

As a noun, a substitute is a person or thing that takes the place of another, like a player who comes on when someone leaves the field. As a verb, it means to use one in place of another.
Example: You can use honey as a substitute for sugar in tea.
Can there be a survivor of a storm without being hurt?

Yes. A survivor is a person who stays alive after a dangerous event, hurt or not. It is a noun.
Example: The only survivor of the storm was a small wooden boat.
What time is teatime exactly?

There is no fixed time. Teatime is the time of day when people usually have tea and a snack, often in the late afternoon. It is a noun.
Example: Grandma calls us in for biscuits at teatime.
Can a word like technical be used for both people and words?

Yes. Technical means connected with the practical skills or special knowledge of a subject or machine. It is an adjective. A technical word is used by experts in a field.
Example: The technical manual explained how to fix the machine.
What is a thimble for?

A thimble is a small cap worn on the finger when sewing to protect it from the needle. It is a noun.
Example: Grandmother pushed the needle through the thick cloth with her thimble.
What kind of weather is tropical?

Tropical means to do with the hot, wet regions near the equator. It is an adjective. Tropical places have warm weather for most of the year.
Example: Bananas and coconuts grow well in the tropical climate of Kerala.
Is triangular only for shapes like roofs and flags?

No, it can describe anything with three sides or in the shape of a triangle. It is an adjective.
Example: The pennant on the bicycle was triangular and bright red.
If I am unlucky today, did I do something wrong?

No. Unlucky means having bad luck, so things go wrong by chance rather than because of anything you did. It is an adjective.
Example: Our team was unlucky when the ball hit the post twice.
How do I show I am unselfish at home?

Unselfish means caring about the needs of others more than your own. It is an adjective. You can show it by sharing, helping and listening.
Example: Ria was unselfish and gave her seat to an old man.
Would it be impolite to call a visitor unwelcome?

It would be unkind to say it to someone's face. Unwelcome means not wanted or not pleasing. It is an adjective.
Example: The unwelcome news about the cancelled trip made everybody sad.
Do you only wrestle in a ring, or can it be a figure of speech?

Both. To wrestle is to fight by grabbing and trying to throw an opponent, as in a sport. It is also used to say that you struggle with a problem. It is a verb.
Example: The two boys wrestled playfully on the soft grass.
My sister called the shopkeeper dishonest. Is that a big accusation?

Yes, it is a serious thing to say about someone. Dishonest means not truthful, ready to lie or cheat. It is an adjective. It is better to say it only when you are sure.
Example: The dishonest seller gave less change than he owed.
